analysis.title: XPO (XPO): 3Q26 EPS Beat; 2026 EBITDA Higher on Cost Leverage; BUY
key_insights: XPO (Buy) reported adjusted 3Q26 EPS from operations of $1.70 versus GS $1.58 and Visible Alpha consensus $1.57. Total adjusted EBITDA was $433mn, about $10mn above the GS forecast of $423mn.
LTL EBITDA was $389mn versus GSe $383mn and Visible Alpha $381mn. LTL revenue of about $1.473bn was in line with GSe of $1.472bn.
Tonnage rose 5% YoY versus GSe 4.5%. Yield ex fuel rose 3.6% YoY versus GSe 4.5%. Management cited mix factors (length of haul and weight) for the slower yield growth and expects better yield in 4Q.

Operating ratio was 80.1% versus GSe 80.5%, which is 20bps better sequentially and 260bps better YoY. Insurance and claims cost was $18m versus GSe $29m, which offset salaries of $720m versus GSe $712m.

Monthly tonnage was +5.8%/+3.7%/+5.4% YoY in July/August/September and shipments per day were +5.9%/+5.7%/+5.7% YoY. Weight per shipment was slightly negative YoY, and shipment growth was fastest in the higher-yielding, higher-margin local channel.

October tonnage was running mid +6% YoY, ahead of normal month-over-month seasonality. Management expects full 4Q tonnage to accelerate from October's 6.5% YoY if normal seasonality holds, helped by easier comps in November and December. October yield is up about 5% YoY.

4Q26 LTL OR is guided to be below 82%, versus the typical 250bps sequential deterioration (180bps at the high end). Full-year OR improvement guidance was raised from more than 200bps YoY to more than 250bps.

GS sees XPO and LTL at large at the start of an upcycle. Industry capacity is about 5% lower in doors than post-COVID, which GS says should support yields. A pickup in the industrial economy could add further acceleration.
Management described volume growth as 2/3 from XPO winning share and 1/3 from the market firming. Retail and industrial customers are slightly positive for 2H26.

GS raised FY26/27/28 EBITDA estimates to $1,580mn/$1,754mn/$1,898mn from $1,545mn/$1,698mn/$1,858mn and EPS estimates to $5.85/$6.85/$7.80 from $5.55/$6.45/$7.50, reflecting stronger tonnage and OR expectations.

The LTL 2.0 plan has four parts: better service (3Q26 claims ratio 0.2% versus about 1% before), network investment with more than 30% excess door capacity, faster yield growth through contract pricing, accessorials and local/SMB share, and cost efficiency from insourcing linehaul miles and labor planning. AI tools are expected to add low-single-digit productivity.

Price target rose to $251 from $247 on about 17.5x EV/EBITDA (from about 18.0x) applied to Q5-Q8 EBITDA of $1,856mn. GS cut the multiple slightly because XPO is moving past what it views as the cyclical bottom for tonnage and earnings. Implied upside from $181.69 is 38.1%.
Longer term, management's goal is an OR in the low 70s, closer to its best-in-class peer.

market_movers.rationale: Buy reiterated after a 3Q26 EPS and EBITDA beat. Target raised from $247 as higher tonnage and OR estimates outweigh a slightly lower 17.5x EV/EBITDA multiple.

sector_views.rationale: GS says LTL appears to be at the start of an upcycle with demand firming. Industry door capacity is about 5% lower than post-COVID, which supports yields.

earnings_insights: XPO 3Q26 adjusted EPS from operations reported at $1.70 versus GS estimate $1.58 and Visible Alpha consensus $1.57.
XPO 3Q26 total adjusted EBITDA reported at $433mn versus GS estimate $423mn. LTL EBITDA reported at $389mn versus GS estimate $383mn and Visible Alpha consensus $381mn.
XPO 3Q26 LTL operating ratio reported at 80.1% versus GS estimate 80.5%, a 260bps YoY improvement versus company parameters of 200bps YoY.
XPO 3Q26 tonnage reported +5% YoY versus GS estimate +4.5%. Yield ex fuel reported +3.6% YoY versus GS estimate +4.5%.

Guidance from the call: 4Q26 LTL OR below 82%, full-year OR improvement now more than 250bps YoY (previously more than 200bps), 4Q yield growth above 3Q's 3.6% and 4Q tonnage above October's preliminary 6.5% YoY.

GS estimates (forecasts, not prints): FY26/27/28 EPS $5.85/$6.85/$7.80 (prior $5.55/$6.45/$7.50) and EBITDA $1,580mn/$1,754mn/$1,898mn (prior $1,545mn/$1,698mn/$1,858mn). Quarterly EPS forecasts are $1.44 for 4Q26E, $1.39 for 1Q27E and $1.95 for 2Q27E.

trade_ideas.description: Long XPO equity, Buy rating, 12-month price target $251
trade_ideas.rationale: OR improvement of more than 250bps in 2026, share gains with SMB shippers, yield growth from mix and accessorials, and an early-stage LTL upcycle.
trade_ideas.risk: Slower economic growth (tariffs or manufacturing slowdown), failure to execute the LTL margin program, pricing not holding in a slower tonnage environment, and difficulty integrating recently purchased service centers.

risk_factors: Slower economic growth than expected, potentially from tariff concerns or a manufacturing slowdown.
Inability to execute on the LTL margin improvement program (longer-term 600bps improvement from pro forma 88% to low 80s by 2027).
LTL pricing or XPO-specific pricing does not hold up in a slower tonnage environment or under the renewed national accounts focus.
Difficulty integrating and ramping the recently purchased LTL service centers.
Yield growth slowed in 3Q on mix (length of haul and weight), and a repeat would cut into the planned yield gains.
